Well: that fault may be mended with a break faſt: read on. That makes amends for her ſoure breath. It's no matter for that; ſo ſhee ſleepe not in her talke. Oh villaine, that ſet this downe among her vices; To be ſlow in words, is a womans onely vertue: I pray thee out with't, and place it for her chiefe vertue. Out with that too: It was Eues legacie, and cannot be t'ane from her. I care not for that neither: becauſe I loue cruſts. Well: the beſt is, ſhe hath no teeth to bite. If her liquor be good, ſhe ſhall: if ſhe will not, I will; for good things ſhould be praiſed. Of her tongue ſhe cannot; for that's writ downe ſhe is ſlow of: of her purſe, ſhee ſhall not, for that ile keepe ſhut: Now, of another thing ſhee may, and that cannot I helpe. Well, proceede. Stop there: Ile haue her: ſhe was mine, and not mine, twice or thrice in that laſt Article: rehearſe that once more. More haire then wit: it may be ile proue it: The couer of the ſalt, hides the ſalt, and therefore it is more then the ſalt; the haire that couers the wit, is more then the wit; for the greater hides the leſſe: What's next? That's monſtrous: oh that that were out. Why that word makes the faults gracious: Well, ile haue her: and if it be a match, as nothing is impoſſible. Why then, will I tell thee, that thy Maſter ſtaies for thee at the North gate. For thee? I, who art thou? he hath ſtaid for a bet ter man then thee. Thou muſt run to him; for thou haſt ſtaid ſo long, that going will ſcarce ſerue the turne. Now will he be ſwing'd for reading my Letter; An vnmannerly ſlaue, that will thruſt himſelfe into ſe crets: Ile after, to reioyce in the boyes correctio ̄ . Marry Sir, I carried Miſtris Siluia the dogge you bad me. Marry ſhe ſaies your dog was a cur, and tels you curriſh thanks is good enough for ſuch a preſent. No indeede did ſhe not: Here haue I brought him backe againe. I Sir, the other Squirrill was ſtolne from me By the Hangmans boyes in the market place, And then I offer'd her mine owne, who is a dog As big as ten of yours, & therefore the guift the greater.
Sir Thurio, feare not, but that ſhe will loue you Now Valentine is baniſh'd from her ſight. This weake impreſſe of Loue, is as a figure Trenched in ice, which with an houres heare Diſſolues to water, and doth looſe his forme. A little time will melt her frozen thoughts, And worthleſſe Valentine ſhall be forgot. How now ſir Protheus, is your countriman (According to our Proclamation) gon? My daughter takes his going grieuouſly? So I beleeue: but Thurio thinkes not ſo: Protheus, the good conceit I hold of thee, (For thou haſt ſhowne ſome ſigne of good deſert) Makes me the better to confer with thee. Thou know'ſt how willingly, I would effect The match betweene ſir Thurio, and my daughter? And alſo, I thinke, thou art not ignorant How ſhe oppoſes her againſt my will? I, and peruerſly, ſhe perſeuers ſo: What might we doe to make the girle forget The loue of Valentine, and loue ſir Thurio ? I, but ſhe'll thinke, that it is ſpoke in hate. Then you muſt vndertake to ſlander him. Where your good word cannot aduantage him, Your ſlander neuer can endamage him; Therefore the office is indifferent, Being intreated to it by your friend. And Protheus, we dare truſt you in this kinde, Becauſe we know (on Valentines report) You are already loues firme votary, And cannot ſoone reuolt, and change your minde. Vpon this warrant, ſhall you haue acceſſe, Where you, with Siluia, may conferre at large. For ſhe is lumpiſh, heauy, mellancholly, And (for your friends ſake) will be glad of you; Where you may temper her, by your perſwaſion, To hate yong Ʋ alentine, and loue my friend. I, much is the force of heauen-bred Poeſie. This diſcipline, ſhowes thou haſt bin in loue. About it Gentlemen. Euen now about it, I will pardon you. How now ſir Protheus ; how now Thurio ? Which of you ſaw Eglamoure of late? Saw you my daughter? Why then She's fled vnto that pezant, Valentine ; And Eglamoure is in her Company: 'Tis true: for Frier Laurence met them both As he, in pennance wander'd through the Forreſt: Him he knew well: and gueſd that it was ſhe, But being mask'd, he was not ſure of it. Beſides ſhe did intend Confeſſion At Patricks Cell this euen, and there ſhe was not. Theſe likelihoods confirme her flight from hence; Therefore I pray you ſtand, not to diſcourſe, But mount you preſently, and meete with me Vpon the riſing of the Mountaine foote That leads toward Mantua, whether they are fled: Diſpatch (ſweet Gentlemen) and follow me.
Since his exile ſhe hath deſpis'd me moſt, Forſworne my company, and rail'd at me, That I am deſperate of obtaining her. Therefore, as you vnwinde her loue from him; Leaſt it ſhould rauell, and be good to none, You muſt prouide to bottome it on me: Which muſt be done, by praiſing me as much As you, in worth diſpraiſe, ſir Ʋ alentine. And thy aduice, this night, ile put in practiſe: Therefore, ſweet Protheus, my direction-giuer, Let vs into the City preſently To ſort ſome Gentlemen, well skil'd in Muſicke. I haue a Sonnet, that will ſerue the turne To giue the on-ſet to thy good aduiſe. How now, ſir Protheus, are you crept before vs? I, but I hope, Sir, that you loue not here. Who, Siluia ? I thanke you for your owne: Now Gentlemen Let's tune: and too it luſtily a while. Where meete we? Farewell. Sir Protheus, what ſaies Siluia to my ſuit?
Fellowes, ſtand faſt: I ſee a paſſenger.
If there be ten, ſhrinke not, but down with 'em. Peace: we'll heare him. Whether trauell you? For what offence? Haue you the Tongues? Tell vs this: haue you any thing to take to? And I from Mantua, for a Gentleman, Who, in my moode, I ſtab'd vnto the heart. Indeede becauſe you are a baniſh'd man, Therefore, aboue the reſt, we parley to you: Are you content to be our Generall? To make a vertue of neceſſity, And liue as we doe in this wilderneſſe? Thou ſhalt not liue, to brag what we haue of fer'd.
Stand ſir, and throw vs that you haue about 'ye. If not: we'll make you ſit, and rifle you. I by my beard will we: for he is a proper man. Haue you long ſoiourn'd there? By the bare ſcalpe of Robin Hoods fat Fryer, This fellow were a King, for our wilde faction. Know then, that ſome of vs are Gentlemen, Such as the fury of vngouern'd youth Thruſt from the company of awfull men. My ſelfe was from Verona baniſhed, For practiſing to ſteale away a Lady, And heire and Neece, alide vnto the Duke. What ſaiſt thou? wilt thou be of our conſort? Say I, and be the captaine of vs all: We'll doe thee homage, and be rul'd by thee, Loue thee, as our Commander, and our King. No, we deteſt ſuch vile baſe practiſes. Come, goe with vs, we'll bring thee to our Crewes, And ſhow thee all the Treaſure we haue got; Which, with our ſelues, all reſt at thy diſpoſe.
That's not ſo, ſir: we are your enemies. Whence came you? What, were you baniſh'd thence? Why nere repent it, if it were done ſo; But were you baniſht for ſo ſmall a fault? We'll haue him: Sirs, a word. And I, for ſuch like petty crimes as theſe. But to the purpoſe: for we cite our faults, That they may hold excus'd our lawleſſe liues; And partly ſeeing you are beautifide With goodly ſhape; and by your owne report, A Linguiſt, and a man of ſuch perfection, As we doe in our quality much want. But if thou ſcorne our curteſie, thou dyeſt. Come, come be patient: We muſt bring you to our Captaine.
Now, my yong gueſt; me thinks your' allyeholly; I pray you why is it? Come, we'll haue you merry: ile bring you where you ſhall heare Muſique, and ſee the Gentleman that you ask'd for. I that you ſhall. Harke, harke. I: but peace, let's heare'm. Who is Siluia? what is ſhe? That all our Swaines commend her? Holy, faire, and wiſe is ſhe, The heauen ſuch grace did lend her, that ſhe might admired be. Is ſhe kinde as ſhe is faire? For beauty liues with kindneſſe: Loue doth to her eyes repaire, To helpe him of his blindneſſe: And being help'd, inhabits there. Then to Siluia, let vs ſing, That Siluia is excelling; She excels each mortall thing Vpon the dull earth dwelling. To her let vs Garlands bring. How now? are you ſadder then you were before; How doe you, man? the Muſicke likes you not. Why, my pretty youth? How, out of tune on the ſtrings. You haue a quicke eare. I perceiue you delight not in Muſique. Harke, what fine change is in the Muſique. You would haue them alwaies play but one thing. I tell you what Launce his man told me, He lou'd her out of all nicke. Gone to ſeeke his dog, which to morrow, by his Maſters command, hee muſt carry for a preſent to his Lady. By my hallidome, I was faſt aſleepe. Marry, at my houſe: Truſt me, I thinke 'tis almoſt day.
This is the houre that Madam Siluia Entreated me to call, and know her minde: Ther's ſome great matter ſhe'ld employ me in. Madam, Madam. Your ſeruant, and your friend; One that attends your Ladiſhips command. As many (worthy Lady) to your ſelfe: According to your Ladiſhips impoſe, I am thus early come, to know what ſeruice It is your pleaſure to command me in. Where ſhall I meete you? I will not faile your Ladiſhip: Good morrow (gentle Lady.)
Madam, I pitty much your grieuances, Which, ſince I know they vertuouſly are plac'd, I giue conſent to goe along with you, Wreaking as little what betideth me, As much, I wiſh all good befortune you. When will you goe? The Sun begins to guild the weſterne skie, And now it is about the very houre That Siluia, at Fryer Patricks Cell ſhould meet me, She will not faile; for Louers breake not houres, Vnleſſe it be to come before their time, So much they ſpur their expedition. See where ſhe comes: Lady a happy euening. Feare not: the Forreſt is not three leagues off, If we recouer that, we are ſure enough.
Where is the Gentleman that was with her? Come, I muſt bring you to our Captains caue. Feare not: he beares an honourable minde, And will not vſe a woman lawleſly.
Being nimble footed, he hath out ▪ run vs. But Moyſes and Valerius follow him: Goe thou with her to the Weſt end of the wood, There is our Captaine: Wee'll follow him that's fled, The Thicket is beſet, he cannot ſcape.
